message.content:
Sure! Here’s a quick example of how you can post that comment to VirusTotal using a simple `curl` command (or you can adapt it to your preferred language).  
Replace **ABC321** with your actual API key if you haven’t already.

```bash
# POST a comment to the IP 192.168.1.1
curl -X POST "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
           "type": "comment",
           "attributes": {
             "text": "Confirmed #malware"
           }
         }'
```

### What this does
- **Endpoint**: `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments` – the API route for adding comments to an IP resource.  
- **Headers**:  
  - `x-apikey`: Your VirusTotal API key.  
  - `Content-Type: application/json`: Indicates the payload is JSON.  
- **Body**: The JSON you supplied, wrapped in single quotes so the shell interprets it correctly.

### Expected response
If everything goes well, you’ll receive a JSON response similar to:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "some-comment-id",
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
      "text": "Confirmed #malware",
      "created_at": "2026-07-07T12:34:56Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-07-07T12:34:56Z"
    }
  }
}
```

### Using Python (optional)
If you prefer Python, here’s a quick snippet:

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"
headers = {
    "x-apikey": "ABC321",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
        "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
}

response = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(response.status_code)
print(response.json())
```

That’s all you need to add the comment. Let me know if you run into any issues!
